    3. Assigning each unique routing key to the least loaded simulator in the current batch.

    4. All requests sharing the same routing key within this batch are routed to the same simulator,

    strict cross-batch deterministic locality (i.e., a given prefix might be routed to different
    simulators in different batches). This strategy is chosen based on the observation that
    a purely random router (which offers strong within-batch load balancing) outperformed
    a deterministic-hashing-based router (which offers strong cross-batch locality but
    can lead to within-batch load imbalance).
